git_commit: registration (this commit), before any code; code and result in later commits
status: REGISTERED, not run. Descriptive planning for the prospective direction shadow track (master plan Phase 3, 5A): no hypothesis is tested, nothing is fitted for use, nothing is selected, nothing in the live system changes.
why: The master plan (Phase 3, 5A) requires an estimate of how much prospective data the direction track needs to detect an effect as small as E032's (Brier about 0.001 better than the base rate) before its checkpoints are set, and forbids promising a definitive answer by 2026-12-14 if the sample cannot support one. E024 and E025 showed this project's checkpoints must be sized by a power study, not by round numbers: the 48h block-bootstrap interval is liberal below about 2,000 hours (E025), and a fixed-size rule can fail a good model by chance (E024).
question: For a prospective record of N consecutive graded hours, how often would the planned test (the paired Brier difference with a 48h circular block-bootstrap 95% interval) show the frozen eight-input model better than the base rate, better than the one-feature rule, and the one-feature rule better than the base rate; how often would it wrongly do so when there is no effect; and how informative are the calibration measures at that size?
data_touched: Development data only: E032's walk-forward out-of-sample predictions, rebuilt exactly as E032 built them (build_frame -> load_bars(end=HOLDOUT.start); identical rows, folds, inputs and C), exploration and validation. No holdout candle (allow_holdout stays False; research/HOLDOUT_ACCESS.log must still not exist afterwards), no buffer hour, no live or prospective outcome. The frozen regime terciles (research/monitoring/regime_terciles_v1.json, development-defined) are read for a descriptive split.

method.reproduction_check_first: The rebuilt predictions must reproduce E032's recorded Brier scores (base rate, model, one feature; both periods) to 5 decimals, or the study stops.
method.per_hour_series: The Brier difference is a mean of per-hour terms, so each comparison is a series: d_MB = (p_B - y)^2 - (p_M - y)^2, d_MF = (p_F - y)^2 - (p_M - y)^2, d_FB = (p_B - y)^2 - (p_F - y)^2 (positive = the second-named is better). M = the eight-input logistic, F = the one-feature logistic (taker_buy_share_1h), B = the leak-free base rate.
method.windows: As E024: every contiguous N-hour window of the out-of-sample record, laid every 168 hours, within each period separately. N in 500, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, 6000, 8000, 10000, 13000 (only where the period is long enough; the number of windows is printed, and windows of a large N overlap heavily, so their shares are less precise than their count suggests).
method.test_per_window: The planned test: the mean of d over the window and its 48h circular block-bootstrap 95% interval (500 resamples per window, seed fixed; the same resampling scheme as agent/research/metrics.block_bootstrap). 'Detects' = the interval's lower end > 0.
method.false_positive_control: The same test on the series centred to a zero mean over its period (d - mean(d)), which keeps the series' autocorrelation and removes the effect. The share of windows whose lower end > 0 is the one-sided false-positive rate (nominal 2.5%).
method.no_improvement_rule_check: For a smallest effect of interest SESOI = 0.0005 (about half of E032's development gains of 0.00094 / 0.00107), the share of windows whose interval's upper end < SESOI: on the real series (a false 'no improvement' when the development effect is true) and on the centred series (a correct 'no improvement' when there is no effect).
method.analytic_cross_check: From each whole period: the block-bootstrap SE of mean(d) scaled by sqrt(n_period / N), and the N for 80% power, n_period * (2.802 * SE_period / mean(d))^2. The simulation and this must broadly agree.
method.calibration_informativeness: Per window, for M: calibration-in-the-large (mean stated - observed UP share) and ECE, on the real outcomes and on outcomes simulated from M's own probabilities (a forecaster perfectly calibrated by construction, seed fixed). The 5th-95th percentile ranges show what a calibration measure can and cannot distinguish at each N.
method.regime_context: Descriptive only: mean(d_MB) per frozen rv_168 tercile (low / mid / high) in each period. The prospective record has so far been entirely in the low tercile, so if the effect lives mainly in other regimes the power figures are optimistic for a calm market.

expectation_stated_in_advance: From E032's whole-period intervals alone (SE about 0.00026 on 13,127 validation hours and 0.00011 on 43,182 exploration hours): about 4,400 (exploration effect) to 5,900 (validation effect) graded hours for 80% power on model vs base rate, i.e. roughly 6 to 8 months of collection, so no definitive answer by 2026-12-14 (the track will then hold about 1,400 hours). Model vs one feature: about 13,000 hours at the exploration effect and about 190,000 at the validation effect, so effectively undecidable prospectively. Below about 2,000 hours the interval is expected to be liberal (E025). Written down so the result is read against what was already computable.
what_this_is_not: It fits nothing for use, chooses no model and changes no rule. It reuses worn development periods, which is acceptable for estimating variability and would not be for choosing anything. It assumes the prospective effect equals the development effect; if the true prospective effect is smaller (validation wear, a frozen single fit instead of a walk-forward), every 'hours needed' figure is an UNDER-estimate, and that is said wherever it is printed.
